utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: The "White House" in the upper photograph is what you see in the centre of the photograph. There's a tree in front of it. After that you see a flat white-like building, and that's called the "White House."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, the photograph below it, are you able to recognise anything in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: That's the same area, but -- yeah. I conclude that I see the "White House" and that same pile is burning. It's probably done from one of our steady OPs in the base, but as the -- no, it's not as detailed and clear as the northern one. When you see in front must be the "White House," and what you see on the left burning is that pile. I can conclude that out of the surroundings, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that the top photograph corresponds more accurately to what you actually saw --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- that day? Now, did you receive any instructions about what to do with the DutchBat archives, the computers and sensitive information and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes. We were ordered by the UN to destroy everything, including our computers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you able to do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: We did not complete that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So can you describe for the Trial Chamber who was left on the base after the transportations were completed?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. We had people of Medecins sans Frontieres, MSF, with patients and wounded; still one of the representatives of the committee; representative of UNHCR; interpreters; and DutchBat, the rest of DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how about the UNMOs? Were they still around, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, of course. The UNMOs and their interpreters as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How about the DutchBat soldiers who you said had been taken prisoner when the OPs fell and had been kept at Bratunac and elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: They were still in Bratunac, never came back to the battalion, and were sent home directly from their location in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You just mentioned some wounded who remained --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: -- in the compound. Were there also wounded located by at that point?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes. There were wounded which we tried to bring out during the evacuation but that transport was stopped and sent back in -- out of the area of Kladanj, and there were wounded of that transport in the hospital of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm going to turn your attention now to the 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In connection with these wounded you just mentioned, did a delegation of VRS and Serb civilian officials arrive at the Potocari compound?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please describe how that came about?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to evacuate the wounded in a normal way, but the military means, a Norwegian medevac company being stationed in the area of Tuzla did not succeed in reaching us to pick up the wounded and bring them out. Then I tried through the MSF to contact the ICRC to do the job, because the Bosnian Serbs told me that I could hand over the wounded absolutely to them. They had hospitals as well. But I didn't think that was a pretty good idea. And so I succeeded in ICRC coming down to pick up the wounded. And that meeting was to coordinate details with the Bosnian Serbs and ICRC, details about the evacuation of the wounded out of Potocari and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And whom did this delegation consist of?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: The head of delegation was Colonel Jankovic. Present was Major Nikolic with body-guard, Major Nikolic, staff officer of the Bratunac Brigade; a lieutenant-colonel whose name I forgot but said that he was a lawyer, a civilian who appeared to be later on the new mayor or something of Srebrenica; and somebody I only can describe as what I call the Mladic look alike. He didn't say anything. He was just there, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Who took the lead?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Colonel Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was there anyone there from the Muslim community?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Not in that stage, because it was concerning the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at some point did one of the Muslim refugees appear, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes, when the arrangement -- I handed over the wounded formally to the ICRC and the mentioned Major Nikolic insisted to inspect the people whether they were still soldiers or -- or what he said criminals between them, so ICRC went down to the hospital together with that Major Nikolic and security squad of DutchBat to do that inspection, and then Colonel Jankovic asked for one of the representatives, Mr. Mandic, to appear because he had a declaration and he would like Mr. Mandic to sign that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you just referred to a declaration. Had you seen this declaration?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes. He just waved with it. I didn't see it -- I couldn't read it when I saw that it was in the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So can you describe for the Trial Chamber what you did next.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes. I had my own interpreters translate it into English, because Jankovic asked me to sign as a witness that Mr. Mandic was not forced to sign it, et cetera, et cetera. So I checked the text and made an alteration.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get to that in a moment. The -- do you generally recall the gist of -- of this declaration?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: In fact, the Serbs wanted -- stated that the evacuation had been performed in a proper, say, a humanitarian way according to all the international law, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could, may we have 65 ter 453 displayed on e-court and, in particular, page 3, please. And could we raise it up and zoom in just a bit, please. And lower it a bit, please. Okay. Actually, can we start at the top a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, would you take a moment and just look at the document, orient yourself, and when you're ready, we'll also look at the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise this as being the field translation that your people did?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, yes. The translation I had made by my interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, there are a series of dashes in the centre of the document, one which begins "The civilian population can remain ..." Do you see that there, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you just read that that portion out loud?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: "Given population can remain in the enclave or evacuate, dependent upon the wish of each individual."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Based on your experience and from what you observed and had reported to you at the time, is this a true statement?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: No. It's nonsense, because they didn't have an opportunity to stay, not a realistic opportunity to stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, moving down --

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Or -- or move in any direction. It was ordered that they should go to the Kladanj area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who ordered that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now moving down one bullet or one dash.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you would just read that portion, please?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: "In the event that we wish to evacuate, it is possible for us to choose the direction of our movement and have decided that the entire population is to evacuate to the territory of the county of Kladanj."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And now you've just answered that to an extent, I think, but is this a true statement?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: No. It was not a decision of the committee; it was an order of Mladic to go to the area of Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And now the third bullet, sir, if you would read that?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: "It has been agreed that the evacuation is to be carried out by the Army and Police of the Republic of Srpska, supervised and escorted by UNPROFOR."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next section?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: "After agreement had been reached, I assert that the evacuation was carried out by the Serb side correctly and the clauses of the agreement had been adhered to."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, are those portions you've just read true statements, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Well, the agreement that it had to be carried out by the army and police of Republic of Srpska is correct, supervising and escorting in theory, but I already told you what actually happened with my escorts so that is not true. And the last sentence: "Evacuation was carried out by the Serb side correctly and the clause of the agreement had been adhered to," is partially true.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then the final sentence beginning "during," if you would read that, please?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yeah. "During the evacuation there were no incidents on either of the sides, and the Serb side has adhered to all the regulations of the Geneva Conventions and the international war law," and I added "as far as convoys actually escorted by UN forces are concerned."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, why did you add that language there, sir?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Because I -- as of the first or the second convoy, I didn't have any control about what happened. Reports of the Pakistan battalion gave that only women, children were coming in later on. So the men were actually taken apart. We had that report about that killing, nine bodies found. So I wanted to in fact neutralise the whole statement by this sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was the reaction of the Serb members of the delegation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Two reactions. Colonel Jankovic smiled a bit and the colonel being a lawyer went almost bananas. He went very angry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in the end, did Colonel Jankovic permit the document to go ahead and be signed with your notation?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you in fact see your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: That is correct. Left lower side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you present when the two other signatories signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT ALEXANDER FRANKEN
utterances.text: Yes, I was there at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that we are right up against the deadline and I estimate that I have maybe 15 minutes of questioning for tomorrow and we will break for today, if we may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. So we adjourn today. Tomorrow I think we are meeting in the morning. Mr. McCloskey, do you wish to address? I forgot. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps we can do that tomorrow. In fact it's probably a better idea. I think both sides were looking for just a little guidance on 92 ter, 89(F) witnesses. We've had some but I think that would be a good issue to address outside the presence of any witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. So we'll deal with that tomorrow morning first thing, first thing before Mr. Franken continues with his testimony. I thank you, and good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of October, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
